hunt:financial.summary:
Bottom line: I found no edge in same-day or T+1 financial and econ markets (excluding crypto) that clears 2-4c a contract after fees for an auto-sent IOC (immediate-or-cancel) order. Wherever a model is compared with the market price at 1-minute resolution, the market comes out equal or better out of sample. This covers 15-minute commodities and FX, hourly S&P/WTI/gold, daily index, commodity, FX and gas brackets, SOFR and ERCOT. The positive results are all structural and small:
(1) A final-seconds sweep of near-certain contracts on the 15-minute series. It made about +0.9 to +1.0c a contract in both the training and test periods. It is below the 2c bar and needs speed.
(2) The Liquidity Incentive Program (LIP) on the fee-free 15-minute series. It pays $20 per window per market. A resting order collects $1.6-4 of reward a window, but adverse selection costs about the same, so the net is about zero within ±$1.3 a window. That comes from 70 windows on one day.
(3) A 1c LIP 'unlock' order on the 15-minute FX windows: +$0.45 to +0.65 a window on EURUSD/USDJPY, with about $4 of collateral and 10 windows per series.
The large-looking LIP pools on the daily gas and FX markets are a trap. Almost all of the unpaid reward sits on sides where a 1c bid is a near-certain loser, and buyers paying 99c sweep those bids within minutes.

Previous attempt: I reused its data and scripts after re-running every one. Its best lead was a 15-minute 'combined fair' model (market mid blended with the digital value implied by futures). It came out +1.7c ±1.2 on the test period. It fails robustness checks: the minute buckets it did not select reverse sign out of sample, FX loses 3.3c, and alternative split dates give -0.5 to +2.6c. On a fresh holdout (Oct 6 06:45-16:00 UTC) it was +4.7c ±4.1 on n=101, which is not significant.

Data and method: public Kalshi API only, through the shared rate limiter at about 2.2 requests per second. No orders, credentials or repo edits, and prod.sqlite was not touched. New this run:
- trade prints for 1,113 sampled 15-minute windows (Sep 8 - Oct 5) plus 70 LIP windows on Oct 6;
- 5-second LIP order-book snapshots, logged from 13:33 UTC Oct 6;
- a fresh 15-minute holdout and fresh Yahoo prices;
- an hourly S&P digital-model study, a gas trend model, an FX daily LIP study with model fair values, and a measure of how long 1c bids survive.

Scripts and outputs are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-samgeng14-Code-kalshi-desk/9a3d63ef-0f2c-4a8c-be2d-105c6d47465f/scratchpad/edge/fin/:
- q15tr/ (an.py, an2.py, an3.py, an4.py, out_*.txt)
- fresh/ (q15_holdout.py, holdout2.txt)
- lip3/ (lipsim.py, lipsim2.py, lipsim3.py, sim2_final.txt, sim3_final.txt)
- lipfx/fxlip.py, lipd/survival.py
- hidx/ (hidx_build.py, hidx_an.py, hidx_fav.py)
- gas2/gas_trend.py
- out/*.txt
- ../fin_skeptic/q15_check7.py

Two loggers started by the previous attempt are still running: lip2/logger.py, a public order-book poller that stops at about 20:33 UTC, and thin/gas_snaplog.py. Both are read-only.

Recommendations:
- Do not give any financial or econ lane auto-send authority at the 2-4c threshold.
- If anything is tried live, run two small measured tests and reconcile the reward from the next day's ledger:
  - (a) LIP-15 on a single FX series, 1c unlock plus resting 2 ticks behind the touch;
  - (b) the final-seconds sweep, gated by a sub-second Pyth distance check.

candidates.name: 15-minute final-seconds near-certain sweep
candidates.markets: KXGOLD15M, KXSILVER15M, KXWTI15M, KXCOPPER15M, KXNATGAS15M, KXPALLADIUM15M, KXPLATINUM15M, KXEURUSD15M, KXGBPUSD15M, KXUSDJPY15M (all fee_type quadratic x1; no maker fee)
candidates.rule: Act only in the last 10 s before the window closes. If either side is offered at 0.97-0.99, buy it with IOC at that ask and hold to settlement. In the last 3 s, 0.97-0.98 is also allowed. Ex-ante: uses only the price and the clock. It also needs a sub-second Pyth guard (skip when the settlement feed is within about 2 sigma-sqrt(tau) of the strike), which I could not test with public data. A minute-bar futures filter added nothing.
candidates.net_edge_cents:
After the taker fee, all 0.97-0.99 prints in the last 10 s: +0.98c a contract (train +1.03, test +0.89).
By cell:
- at 0.99 in the last 10-3 s: +0.89 train / +0.93 test
- at 0.99 in the last 3 s: +0.85 / +0.92
- at 0.97-0.98 in the last 3 s: +1.80 / +2.03
- at 0.97-0.98 in the 10-3 s cell: about 0 (+0.43 ±1.42 / -0.01 ±1.54)
- above 0.995: +0.13
Compare the 2-4c auto-send bar: none of these cells clears it.
candidates.n_and_se:
1,113 sampled windows (652 train, Sep 8-26; 461 test, Sep 27 - Oct 5).
- 452k contracts printed at 0.97-0.99 in the last 10 s, in 390 windows.
- Window-clustered SE: ±0.02-0.06c for the 0.99 cells, ±0.2c for the 3 s cell at 0.97-0.98.
- Tail risk: 0.385% of contracts lost, in 10 of 1,113 windows (natgas, copper, gold, WTI). The break-even loss rate at an average price of 0.98 is about 1.9%.
- Widening the window costs edge: in the last 60 s, 0.97-0.99 was -1.03c in train (a 2.4% gold loss) and 0.90-0.97 was -5.0c in train.
candidates.out_of_sample: Yes. The sign and size hold from train (Sep 8-26) to test (Sep 27 - Oct 5). A third sample of 63 Oct 6 LIP-series windows (copper, platinum, palladium, natgas, EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY) gave +1.39c a contract with 0.028% lost.
candidates.capacity: About 400 contracts a window were printed at 0.97-0.99 in the last 10 s, worth about $3-4.7 a window to all takers combined; such prints appeared in about 35% of windows. These prints were taken by existing bots, so our share is unknown and depends on latency. Capital recycles: settlement comes 7-30 s after close.
candidates.execution: Taker IOC. The whole edge is a latency race in the final seconds, which a 50-100 ms desk on a home connection may lose to colocated bots. It needs a Pyth Hermes stream for the distance guard. It is below the desk's 2-4c threshold, so it would need its own lane at about 0.8c with a strict per-window size cap.
candidates.caveats: This is a picking-up-pennies profile: one loss costs about 98c a contract. Ten loss windows in 1,113 means a full-size $200 position could lose about $200 in one window. Effectively one effect measured on one month.

candidates.name: 15-minute metals 'combined fair' taker (market mid blended with the futures-implied digital value)
candidates.markets: KXGOLD15M, KXSILVER15M, KXWTI15M, KXCOPPER15M, KXNATGAS15M, KXPALLADIUM15M, KXPLATINUM15M
candidates.rule: Fair = logistic(a + b·logit(mid) + c·logit(Φ(z))), where z = ln(F_t/F_open)/(σ_1m·√(15-minute)). F is the futures 1-minute close and σ is taken from the prior 60 minutes. The model is fit per minute bucket (3-5 and 6-9) on training data. Take YES at the ask or NO at 1 - bid when fair - price - taker fee ≥ 1c.
candidates.net_edge_cents:
Metals, 1c threshold:
- train: +1.07c ±0.89
- test (Sep 27 - Oct 5): +1.69c ±1.21
- fresh holdout (Oct 6 06:45-16:00 UTC): +4.7c ±4.1
2c threshold: test +2.8c ±2.2. 3-4c threshold: test +0.5 ±5.2 (n=119) and +3.9 ±8.9 (n=43). That is too few trades and too noisy.
candidates.n_and_se: Train 4,078 trades; test 1,936 trades in 400 clock windows. SE is clustered by clock window across series, and is similar clustered by day or by day-block bootstrap (P(mean ≤ 0) = 0.004 on test). Holdout n=101 in 28 clock windows.
candidates.out_of_sample: Fails robustness. Other split dates give +0.2, -0.5, +1.1, +1.9 and +2.6c. The minute buckets not selected reverse out of sample: 10-12 goes from +2.1 to -0.5 and 13-14 from +3.5 to -3.9. FX is -3.3c ±2.0. The pure digital model loses to the market in Brier at every minute (taker -1 to -2.6c in train, about 0 in test). With the futures price lagged 60 s the result is +0.9 ±1.4, so this is a same-minute race, not slow incorporation.
candidates.capacity: Books are 1-2c wide with hundreds to thousands of contracts at the touch on gold, WTI and copper. Each signal is worth only about 1-2c.
candidates.execution: Taker IOC within about 1 s of a Pyth/futures move. Not suitable for the 2-4c auto-send rule. At most a paper-trade monitor.
candidates.caveats: Selected after looking at the data: the previous attempt picked the 3-9 minute buckets and the 1c threshold after seeing the results. Treat it as unproven.

candidates.name: LIP-15 resting maker (paid quoting on fee-free 15-minute windows)
candidates.markets: KXEURUSD15M, KXGBPUSD15M, KXUSDJPY15M, KXNATGAS15M, KXPLATINUM15M, KXPALLADIUM15M, KXCOPPER15M. LIP terms: $20 per window per market, target 300, discount 0.5, every 15 minutes around the clock, a pool of about $13.4k a day.
candidates.rule: Minutes 0-10 of each window. Rest q per side, post-only, 2 ticks behind the best bid on both YES and NO; re-post after fills; inventory cap 2q.
candidates.net_edge_cents:
Measured as dollars per window, not cents per contract.
- q=60, 2 ticks behind: LIP $1.85; 234 fills a window; 60-s markout -0.74c a contract. Net +$0.12 ±1.35 a window (settlement-valued +$6.5 ±3.8).
- q=30, joining the touch: LIP $1.57; 361 fills; markout -0.99c. Net -$2.00 ±1.22 (settlement-valued +$3.1 ±2.7).
- q=100, 2 ticks behind: net +$1.04 ±1.99 (60-s markout basis).
- Quoting only minutes 0-5: -$1.7 ±0.9.
candidates.n_and_se: 70 market-windows (7 series × 10) on Oct 6, 13:30-16:00 UTC. Fills are counted only where trades printed through our price, or at our price beyond the queue that was ahead. The reward uses the published scoring on 5-second public snapshots, with the $1 minimum payout applied. SE is across windows.
candidates.out_of_sample: There is no training/test split: one afternoon only, with nothing tuned beyond picking the policy grid.
candidates.capacity: Collateral about $30-57 per series. The reward share is about 10-40% at q=30-60, so one series would earn roughly $1.6-4 a window in reward before adverse selection.
candidates.execution: Resting post-only orders with 5-15 s expiry, refreshed every snapshot. It needs fills and cancels from the private WebSocket, and should pull quotes on underlying moves (not simulated, which would improve the result).
candidates.caveats: The 60-s markouts are negative while settlement-valued P&L is positive, and 70 windows cannot tell which is right. Kalshi's actual scoring implementation can't be verified from public data. A live one-series test with ledger reconciliation is the only real check.

candidates.name: LIP 1c 'unlock' on 15-minute FX windows
candidates.rule: Whenever one side of the book holds fewer than 300 contracts, the window's reward is unpaid (excluded). Rest 300 at 1c on that side, but only if the opposite best bid is below 0.99, so the order does not cross. That makes the snapshot count, and our order sets the reference price. Hold any fill to settlement.

Per window, net of 1c-fill losses at settlement:
- EURUSD: +$0.45 ±0.28 (60-s markout basis +$0.94)
- USDJPY: +$0.65 ±0.28
- GBPUSD: -$0.09 ±0.41
- metals: -$0.1 to -$0.9
There is no meaningful cents-a-contract edge: the income is reward.
candidates.n_and_se: 10 windows per series on Oct 6, 13:30-16:00 UTC. SE is across windows.
candidates.capacity: About $4 of collateral per series. The upside is roughly $40-60 a day per FX series if the result held all day, which I doubt: exclusions concentrate late in a window, when 1c bids become sure losers.
candidates.execution: Resting 1c bids, cancelled when the side becomes a near-certain loser in the final minutes.

hunt:financial.nulls:
These are all null or negative out of sample. Fees are included and trades are taken at the quoted ask or bid. The training/test split is noted on each item.

15-minute series (Sep 8 - Oct 5, 12,655 windows, 1-minute candles):
- Market-only price bands: takers lose 1-5c in every band. The 0.97-1.00 band in minutes 10-14 is about 0. The calibration slope b is about 1.0 by minute and by series.
- Digital value from futures alone: worse Brier than the market at every minute. Taker -1 to -2.6c in train, -0.4 ±0.6 in test.
- First minutes: the previous window's direction (momentum or reversal) taken at minutes 1-3 gives -3.6c / -2.8c (n=14k). P(same direction) = 0.494 ±0.004.
- Trade prints (1,113 windows): takers in the first 60 s lose 3.6 / 2.1c (train/test) and average makers make +2.0 / +0.4c. FX makers lose about 2c mid-window in the LIP era.
- Lead-lag: the Kalshi mid co-moves with same-minute futures (r 0.71-0.86 on metals). Lagged correlations are about 0, so there is no slow incorporation to exploit at 1-minute resolution.
- Ties: 0-2.7% of windows. The YES rate is 0.48-0.51, with no tie premium mispriced.

Hourly markets:
- Hourly S&P (KXINXU), 140 events: the digital model from the cash index (^GSPC) loses 2-12c. Market Brier is better at 10 minutes or more before the hour. Market-only bands range from -0.7 to -13c. Blending model and market gave +2 to +5c with SE ±4-8, not significant.
- Hourly WTI (KXWTIH): +9 ±5c 30 minutes before the hour, but -0.4c at 15 minutes and -1.2c at 5 minutes.
- Hourly gold (KXGOLDH): about 0.

Daily brackets:
- S&P and Nasdaq close: -4 to -24c.
- WTI (ICE settlement), gold and silver: -1.5 to -6c.
- Buying favourites at 0.90-0.99, 2-60 minutes before close, across 15 daily series (59k rows): -0.1 to -18c.

Gas (AAA national, diesel, 30 states):
- An AR(1) trend model on daily changes (lag-1 r = 0.75) is far worse than the market: Brier 0.20-0.23 against 0.09-0.11. The market evidently sees intraday retail prices. Taker -5 to -9c.
- The 'side already ahead of yesterday's value' favourite rule on the national market made +2.3c on test (Sep 16 - Oct 5, no losses in 20 days). It lost 2-17c in Aug - mid-Sep with real losses, so it depends on the regime.
- 99c sweeps of 1c bids: 0 losses over 11 events, but the same regime risk, and fast bots take them.

Other daily econ series:
- SOFR daily: the model loses 7-13c.
- ERCOT daily peak: 'lock' sides are already priced at 99c.

Daily LIP unlock (gas, FX, Treasury, SOFR, ERCOT):
- The static payout looks large, for example $40 over the final 7 h across 15 EURUSD markets. Almost all of it is on sure-loser sides.
- 1c-maker fills within 8 h of close historically lose 0.75-1.0c each.
- Today 47% of national-gas volume (32k contracts in 3.6 h) was 1c bids swept by buyers at 99c.
- 1c bids posted on a national-gas loser side survive a median 3.6 minutes. Break-even survival is about 3 h for gas and about 19 h for EURUSD.
- The safe part (a 1c bid only where the model fair is at least 3c) earns about $0.5 an hour across the 15 EURUSD markets and about $0 on USDJPY.
- Farmers already rest 5-10k contracts at 1c on the favourite sides.

Polymarket US: it has no same-day or T+1 financial or econ markets (all its finance and macro events are long-dated), so there are no pairs to trade.

Not testable with public data: a sub-second latency edge in the last minute of the 15-minute windows (it needs historical Pyth ticks); the prints only show that someone already takes those trades.

candidates.name: Women's college basketball (KXNCAAWBGAME) in-game stale-quote IOC after scoring runs, driven by an ESPN score feed and a 5-coefficient logistic fair value
candidates.rule: Universe: KXNCAAWBGAME two-way game markets (series fee_type 'quadratic', multiplier 1, no maker fee). Ex-ante inputs only. (1) Prior p0 = Kalshi effective mid of the home team at the last 1-minute close at or before the scheduled tip, where effective bid = max(home YES bid, 1 - away YES ask) and effective ask = min(home YES ask, 1 - away YES bid); require spread <= 15c (true for ~88% of games). (2) Game state from ESPN play-by-play taken in feed order: home margin m and seconds left (4 x 10-minute quarters; OT = clock), with a play counted as visible only at the running maximum of wallclocks so far (late-inserted plays dropped). (3) Fair f = logistic(0.121*m/sqrt(tau+0.01) + 0.864*logit(p0)*sqrt(tau) + 0.157*logit(p0) - 0.001*m - 0.041), tau = seconds_left/2400 clipped to [0,1.25]; coefficients fit on 1,964 ESPN games before 2026-02-01 (refit reproduces them). (4) Every minute, using the state visible at least L seconds earlier (L = 45 base, 90 conservative): if f - ask - 0.07*ask*(1-ask) >= 0.10, send an IOC to buy home (home YES at the ask or away NO, whichever is cheaper); symmetric for selling home at the effective bid. One order per side per contiguous signal run; only while in-game cumulative volume so far < 20,000 contracts (ex-ante thinness filter). Conservative variant also requires the same-or-better quote to have been present at the previous minute close. $5 clip, $10 per game cap, hold to settlement. Fees: 0.07*C*p*(1-p) rounded up to the cent per order.
candidates.markets: KXNCAAWBGAME, Nov 2026 - Mar 2027 season (no games until Nov 2-3, 2026). Last season: 4,062 settled games over 126 days; 61% traded <= 60k contracts in total and 39% <= 20k; median 21 listed games per day (about 45/day in Jan-Feb, 29/day in Nov, 21/day in Dec). About 60% of thin games produce at least one signal, 1.8 signals per game.
candidates.net_edge_cents: Hold-out (2026-02-01 to 03-23), all 322 games with a prior, cumq<20k filter: L=45: +13.9c per contract; L=90: +11.7c; L=120: +10.5c. Conservative (L=90 and quote also present at the previous minute close): +16.0c. Ex-post thin games (<=60k total volume, 234 games): +16.5c at L=45; executed at the WORST price of the following minute instead of the minute-close quote: +10.3c. By side: buying the team that just extended its lead +20.0c (n=315), buying the trailer +1.9c (n=74). Edge decays with staleness: L=300s +5.8c, L=600s 0.0c, L=900s -2.4c. Liquid games (>60k): -0.5c +/- 10.6 (no edge where there is competition). Dollar terms at $5 clips/$10 cap: $1.93 per game (base) and $1.49 per game (conservative) over all 322 hold games; in-panel per-day mean $17 (sd $39, 7 of 36 days negative) base and $13 (sd $29, 5 of 36 negative) conservative; worst day -$28.
candidates.n_and_se: Independent verifier panel (rebuilt from raw Kalshi 1-minute candles + trades and raw ESPN plays, not the hunter's code). Base L=45: 491 signals, 165 of 322 games, SE clustered by game 2.8c (t about 5); clustered by game day (24-36 days) SE about 3.3c. Conservative: 389 signals, 134 games, +16.0 +/- 3.1c. Thin hold: 416 signals, 141 of 234 games, +16.5 +/- 2.7c; $5-clip $/game 2.57 +/- 0.65, cluster bootstrap 5-95% $1.58-3.69, P(total<=0) ~0. Tune period (Nov 2025 - Jan 2026, 345 thin games) gave the same magnitude: +14.8 +/- 2.6c. Realized P&L rises with model edge bucket (edge 10-15c: +11.2c; 15-20c: +20.3c; 20-30c: +36.5c; 30-50c: +44.6c). Placebos on hold thin: no score information (fair = p0) -4.4 +/- 3.1c; flipped margin -20.5 +/- 2.5c; price-only buy-the-favourite-at-ask control -2.6 +/- 2.9c (n=267). Brier on hold rows (L=45): model 0.1009, Kalshi mid 0.1139, ESPN live WP 0.0995, pregame 0.162. Data integrity: 30 re-pulled games matched the stored trades 19,234/19,234 and candles 8,000/8,000; two signals smell-tested end to end against raw ESPN plays and raw candles (orientation and timing correct; 156 and 113 contracts were taken by others at the same stale price within 2-3 minutes).
candidates.out_of_sample: Model coefficients fit only on ESPN games before 2026-02-01; the rule evaluated on games from 2026-02-01 onward (322 games with a Kalshi prior, 36 game days, Feb 1 - Mar 23 2026) and separately on Nov-Jan (same sign and size). The hunter's independent panel (different ESPN backbone method) gives thin hold +16.7 +/- 2.7c, matching the verifier's +16.5 +/- 2.7c. All L in 20-120 and thr in 0.10-0.20 are positive on hold-out, so the parameter choice is not doing the work. Not yet tested on the 2026-27 season (starts Nov 2-3).
candidates.capacity: Lower bound from prints: in 64% of signals other takers printed >=1 contract at our price or better on our side within (T-60s, T+120s]; 47% >=5; 41% >=10; median 4 contracts. Capping each fill at those prints gives $0.88/game (base) and $0.80/game (conservative) vs $1.93/$1.49 with full $5 clips; print-weighted edge 10-14c per contract. Capital: positions are held to settlement (1-3 h); peak concurrent capital on a hold day was median $7-10, max $128-133 for the panel's ~9 games/day. Scaling to the full universe (~30 thin games/day in Jan-Feb, ~12-14 in Nov-Dec) would need $300-600 at the $10 cap, so with ~$170 systematic cash expect to cover 10-15 games/day: roughly $15-25/day full-clip and $7-12/day prints-capped in Jan-Feb, about half that in Nov-Dec, with daily SD of the same order as the mean and very skewed (one day, Feb 14, was 30% of the conservative variant's hold-out P&L; top 10% of games = 49% of P&L; 37 of 141 traded games lost).
candidates.execution: Taker IOC at the shown effective ask/bid, because the edge is a quote that has not moved for minutes after a scoring run and others take the same quote within 2 minutes; a resting order would miss the stale side and be adverse-selected (Kalshi-only momentum/fade and sibling-stale rules are negative). Speed is not the constraint: L=120 still earns +10.5c and L=300 +5.8c, so a 1-2 minute path (ESPN poll every 3-5 s plus a normal send) is enough; 50-100 ms is unnecessary here. Edge threshold 10c (not 2-4c): the 5-10c bucket is only marginally positive and fee+spread eat it.
candidates.caveats: (1) One season of data; hold-out is 36 game days; results are skewed to a few games and days. (2) Minute-candle granularity: the IOC is assumed to hit the minute-close quote; quote size and sub-minute flicker are unobservable (the worst-price-next-minute execution and the previous-close-quote filter bracket this at +10 to +16c). (3) ESPN real-time publication latency for WBB small-conference games is unmeasured; wallclocks are scorer-entry stamps (whole seconds, 27% duplicates, lag the game clock by a median 1 s, 90th pct 13 s) and other sports showed ~40 s publication delay, so treat L=90-120 (+10.5 to +11.7c, $1.8-2.2/game) as the realistic baseline, not L=45. (4) Nothing can be traded or live-verified until Nov 2, 2026; the market may be more efficient in 2026-27 (edge was zero in liquid games), so the ex-ante cumq<20k filter is essential. (5) ESPN's own live win probability as the fair value is worse at thr 0.10 (+9.5 +/- 3.0c) and similar at 0.15 (+17.5 +/- 3.6c); the simple logistic needs no ESPN WP. (6) Kalshi's own free Sportradar game-state feed might be faster than ESPN; untested. (7) First-week live measurements that decide it: IOC fill rate at the shown price, realized vs model edge on >=50 fills, ESPN state-visible-time minus Kalshi quote-move time per scoring run.

candidates.name: Finnish Liiga hockey (KXLIIGAGAME) goal-triggered IOC from the liiga.fi API goal log (weak, unconfirmed)
candidates.rule: Prior: Kalshi effective home mid at the last minute close before the start (spread <= 15c). Home scoring share s solved from a Poisson in-game model (lambda = 5.35 regulation goals per game, P(OT decided by a goal) = 0.675, both from the 2025-26 Liiga season only) so that P(home wins | 0-0, full game) = p0. Event: a goal appears in liiga.fi/api/v2/games/{season}/{id} goalEvents with its logTime (the 2026-27 feed stamps logTime 3 h early; add 3 h). At the first minute boundary >= logTime + 15 s, compute f = P(home win | current score, regulation time left from the goal's gameTime advanced at 0.58 game-s per wall-s, capped at the period end), and buy the scoring team's side IOC at the shown effective ask if f - ask - 0.07*ask*(1-ask) >= 0.05. Hold to settlement. $5 clip, $10 per game cap.
candidates.markets: KXLIIGAGAME (no maker fee): 83 events on 20 days in Sep-Oct 2026, median 4 games/day (90th pct 7), 1.3k-5k contracts per game; games at about 11:30-13:30 ET on weekdays.
candidates.net_edge_cents: 2026-27 season so far (Sep 1 - Oct 3, 2026): +16.3c per contract at L=15 thr=0.05 (L=60: +15.1c; thr=0.10: +14.9c), 92% win rate, median cost 79c; executed at the worst price of the next minute +12.4c. $0.84 per game at $5 clips ($0.59 prints-capped). But: the price-only control (buy the favourite at the ask at fixed times, no feed) was +7.6 +/- 3.1c this season vs -9.5 +/- 4.0c last season, so the test window was favourite-friendly; realized exceeded the model-implied edge by 6c; 2025-26 (Feb-May 2026, credible goal timestamps only): +0.1 +/- 8.9c (n=25, null). Markout after fill: 1 min -2.9c, 5 min +0.6c, 15 min +4.3c, 30 min +8.1c (the market drifts toward the model slowly; roughly half the settlement P&L is outcome luck). Periodic scan >= 5 min after the last goal: +2.0 +/- 2.2c (null), so any edge is only in the minutes after a goal.

hunt:college.nulls: College baseball (KXNCAABBGAME, Feb-Jun 2026, 468 games with ESPN at-bat states, model fit before Apr 16 and tested on 316 later games): +5.7 +/- 2.8c per contract at L=60 thr=0.10 but -$0.44 +/- 0.37 per game in dollars at $5 clips, because the dollar-weighted cheap trailer contracts lose; on hold rows the model's Brier equals the market mid's (0.1382 both), so there is no information edge; ESPN wallclocks there are 12-hour ambiguous and needed repair. Women's college volleyball (KXNCAAWVMATCH, 275 matches Sep 18 - Oct 5 2026, median ~600 contracts a match): ESPN publishes no play-by-play (plays = 0), so no ex-ante feed rule can be backtested; Kalshi-only rules are null or negative on the later half (sibling-stale minute-close -1.7 +/- 3.5c; any-state sibling -2.2 +/- 3.7c; tape sibling -2.4 +/- 3.1c; momentum -3.7 to -5.9c; fade -8.5 to -10.7c; 22 one-minute buy-both locks of 1.4c median). College hockey: ESPN has no play-by-play; last season's KXNCAAHOCKEYGAME (3-way with a shootout/tie market, 95 games loaded) had essentially no in-game book (median in-game spread 82c, median 10 in-game orders and 1.6k contracts per game), momentum and fade both lose 5-30c, and only 1-3 n-way lock minutes in 95 games; this season's KXNCAAHGAME has 14 events at a median 400 contracts. Other thin daily hockey leagues: AHL (703 events, median 3.4k contracts, ~4 games/day; a 20-game candle sample shows a median in-game spread of 23c and 2.4k in-game contracts), SHL, KHL, DEL, Swiss NL (1.5k-3.3k contracts a game, 2-4 games/day) have wide, thin in-game books and no free timestamped goal feed was identified (HockeyTech gives game time only), so no ex-ante rule was tested. Kalshi-only in-game rules in every league (momentum, fade, sibling-market staleness, cross-market locks) are null or negative after fees; the in-game information has to come from outside the tape. Post-final 'buy the winner before settlement' produced one signal in the WBB hold-out (-1c): these markets close or reprice at the final. Liquid WBB games (>60k contracts) show no edge (-0.5 +/- 10.6c), so the effect lives only where nobody is quoting actively. ESPN live win probability as the fair value is no better than the simple logistic. Maker variants were not credited: the edge decays within minutes and the stale quotes are taken by others, so resting would miss it.
hunt:college.summary: The previous attempt's data and scripts were sound and I re-ran them end to end rather than trusting the saved numbers: a 30-game re-pull reproduced the stored Kalshi trades and candles exactly, the independent verifier panel reproduces the hunter's panel to within 0.2c, and two signals checked against raw ESPN plays and raw candles are correctly oriented and timed. One candidate survives every test I could throw at it: in thin women's college basketball games, after a scoring run the resting quotes sit unchanged for minutes, and an IOC at the shown price for the team that just extended its lead earns about +10 to +16c per contract after fees on the Feb-Mar 2026 hold-out (SE about 3c, 134-165 of 322 games, 36 game days), with the realistic lag band (L = 90-120 s) at +10.5 to +11.7c. Placebos fail as they should (no score information -4c, flipped margin -20c, price-only favourite control -3c), the edge decays to zero by 10 minutes of staleness, it is absent in liquid games, and the model's Brier beats the thin Kalshi mid (0.101 vs 0.114). In dollars at $5 clips with a $10 per-game cap it is $1.5-1.9 per game (full clip) and $0.8-0.9 per game when fills are capped at what others actually printed at that price within 2 minutes; at $170 of systematic cash covering 10-15 games a night that is roughly $15-25 a day in Jan-Feb (prints-capped lower bound $7-12), about half that in Nov-Dec, with daily SD of the same order as the mean, 5-7 losing days in 36, and heavy skew (one day was 30% of the hold-out P&L). It cannot be traded or live-verified until the season starts on Nov 2, 2026, and the 2026-27 market may be more efficient, so the plan should be: record ESPN play-by-play (3-5 s polls, time-stamped on receipt) and Kalshi books for every WBB game from Nov 2, measure ESPN's visible-time lag against Kalshi's quote moves and the IOC fill rate at shown prices in the first week at $2 clips, and scale to $5 only if realized edge on 50+ fills is within a few cents of the model's. Liiga hockey shows the same shape (+16c on 79 signals this season) but fails the prior-season and favourite-luck controls and is worth at most $2-3 a day; keep it as a cheap add-on to record, not a build. Everything else in this hunt is null: college baseball has no information edge, volleyball and college hockey have no free play-by-play feed (and hockey has no in-game book), the minor European and AHL hockey leagues have wide thin books and no timestamped goal feed, and every Kalshi-only in-game rule loses after fees. Latency is not the lever in this corner of the market; a score feed and a 10c edge floor are. hunt:weather.summary:
DAILY WEATHER (Kalshi KXHIGH*/KXLOW* daily temperature brackets, 24 US cities): NO FORECAST-BASED EDGE EXISTS; the market beats every free forecast at every decision time. The only edges that survive held-out testing are two STRUCTURAL maker edges on the observation afternoon, worth about 1-2c per contract (below the desk's 2-4c IOC threshold, so they are resting-order lanes, not IOC lanes), roughly $2/day at 5 contracts per fill with $100-140 of collateral tied up overnight.

WHAT I REUSED AND RE-VERIFIED. The interrupted attempt left three layers (hunter edge/weather, hunter v2 edge/weather2, and an independent verifier edge/verify-weather + v3). I re-ran every local analysis (printed results were lost) and verified the data independently with new code under edge/weather3/: (1) spotcheck_v3.py re-derived 900 random panel rows (300 each from p_live, p_pre, p_hv) from the raw hourly candles and raw IEM METAR CSVs with my own parser: 0 mismatches on quote, next-hour trade high, settlement label, decision time and the running-max floor. (2) tape_check.py: the candle-based maker fill flag agreed with the public trade tape on 180/180 sampled TEST decisions. (3) cli_vs_settle.py: settlement source check over 4,423 settled station-days. (4) fwd_refresh.py: a true forward day (Oct 6, settled this morning, ~50 public requests at 0.5 req/s). Panels: live API Aug 1-Oct 5 (1,529 events, all brackets), historical API Apr 10-Jul 31 (complete brackets Apr 16-Jun 30, tail brackets only otherwise), Jan 15-Apr 9 tail brackets, a random 2025 sample of 52 events for the 7 original cities. Split: PRE Apr 10-Jun 30 / TUNE Jul 1-Sep 5 / TEST Sep 6-Oct 5 (rules were frozen on TUNE before TEST was built), plus Oct 6 forward.

SETTLEMENT SOURCE AND ROUNDING. Rules: 'maximum temperature recorded at <city> (CLIxxx) ... according to The Weather Company', whole degrees F, NWS climate day = local STANDARD-time midnight to midnight (markets close 05:00Z for Eastern cities), settled ~8 AM ET next day. Bracket semantics verified on 4,425 events: exactly one YES bracket per event, settled value always inside it; 'between 66-67' = 66<=H<=67, 'less than 66' = H<=65, 'greater than 73' = H>=74. TWC vs NWS CLI: 4,422 of 4,423 station-days agree (Jan-Oct 2026, 24 stations), plus 24/24 on Oct 6. The ONE disagreement is material: KXHIGHMIA-26AUG29 settled 90 (TWC) while the NWS CLI says 85 and the METAR max was 84.9F; the 90-91 bracket paid, the <88 favorite (quoted 95-98c) lost 100c. So settlement-source risk is ~1 in 4,400 city-days but costs a full dollar per contract when it hits (it is 1 of rule B's 7 pooled losses). Polymarket US settles the same 5 cities on the NWS CLI, so that day would have resolved oppositely across venues. Fees: all 24 KXHIGH series are fee_type quadratic x1 (no maker fee); taker 0.07*p*(1-p) rounded up per order (0.2c at 97c on a 5-lot).

LIQUIDITY AND BRACKET SUMS. Live snapshot 2026-10-07 06:22Z (342 books, 57 events): sum of best YES bids median 0.95 (p10 0.67, p90 1.02), sum of best YES asks median 1.08 (p10 1.05, p90 1.25); 9 next-day events had bid sums of 1.01-1.02, which is below the ~5c of taker fees on a 6-leg sell-all, so no lock. Across 44k historical snapshots (weather2/bsum): ask-sum median 1.08, bid-sum median 0.94; after exact taker fees only 21 buy-all and 23 sell-all 'arbs' of 0.01-4.7c appeared (all on 1-minute-stale hourly closes, mostly <0.5c) - no bracket-sum edge. Favorite band depth 96-99c at 2 AM: 3 YES asks (median 50 contracts); tails 1-4c: 162 offers, median 174 contracts, with 100k-280k-contract 1c offers on already-decided brackets.

candidates.name: A. Afternoon far-tail NO maker (sell YES on brackets the day can no longer reach cheaply)
candidates.rule: Kalshi KXHIGH daily-high brackets, 24 US cities. At each local hour 13:00-18:00 on the observation day D: compute floor = round(max METAR temperature so far in the NWS climate day, using routine+special METARs valid at least 10 min earlier and 6-hour max groups inside the day). For every bracket whose LOWEST winning temperature is strictly above the floor (the day must still warm into it), if the book is two-sided and the YES ask is 2-5c: rest a post-only NO bid at (1 - ask + 1c) when the spread is >= 2c (i.e. offer YES one tick inside the ask), else join at 1 - ask. Fill is counted only if a YES trade printed strictly through the offered price within the hour. One fill per bracket-day; hold NO to settlement. No model, no forecast.

verdicts.name: WBB in-game: take thin-book quotes that are far from a live score model (IOC)
verdicts.reasoning:
I rebuilt the whole test with my own code, not the hunters' book.py or build_v2.py. The stored data is sound: I re-pulled 30 random holdout games from the public API and the store matched exactly (19,234 trades, 8,000 one-minute candles), and 26 re-pulled ESPN games matched play for play (12,198 plays). Missing one-minute candles really are minutes with no change: every trade falls in a minute that has a candle, candle volume equals trade volume, and after every gap the next open equals the previous close (5,380 of 5,380). Refitting the model on ESPN games before Feb 1 (1,964 games) gives [0.120, 0.862, 0.164, 0.001, -0.050], the stated coefficients. Fees are confirmed (quadratic, multiplier 1, no maker fee).

For the score state I used a stricter no-look-ahead version than the hunters': I dropped late-inserted plays (0.87%) and treated each play as visible only from the cumulative-max wallclock. Holdout, thin games, L=45 s, 10c threshold: 16.5 ± 2.7c a contract, 416 trades in 141 of 234 games, $2.57 ± 0.65 a game at a $5 clip and $1.59 ± 0.40 at a $2 clip. The hunters had 16.7c and $2.65.

Attempts to break it:
(1) Placebos behave as real score information should. With the score 5 min old the edge is 5.8 ± 2.9c; at 10 min it is 0.0 ± 2.4c. A constant pregame fair value loses 4.4c. Flipping the margin sign loses 20.5c.
(2) The bigger the predicted edge, the bigger the realized one: 11c, 20c, 36c and 45c across predicted-edge buckets 10-15c, 15-20c, 20-30c and 30-50c. The realized edge (16.5c) is close to what the model predicted (14.8c), and the win rate is 69.7% against 68% predicted, so it does not depend on luck. A price-only rule that buys the in-game favourite has no edge (tune +1.8 ± 2.1c, holdout -2.6 ± 2.9c).
(3) No look-ahead from ESPN timestamps. In liquid games the Kalshi price moves about 49% of the way within 15 s after the ESPN wallclock and 78% within 60 s; in thin games it moves 12% by 60 s and 54% by 5 min.
(4) No post-game or after-close artifacts: 1 signal after the final play and 0 after the market's close_time.
(5) Not phantom quotes. Trades where another taker traded at our price or better in the window from 1 min before to 2 min after the signal earn 17.2 ± 3.2c; trades without such a print earn 15.4 ± 4.0c.
(6) A thinness split known before the game also works: games with pregame volume below the median earn 16.9 ± 2.8c and $2.44 a game. All holdout games under the in-game volume filter alone earn 13.9 ± 2.8c and $1.93 a game.
(7) Independence: clustering by game day (17 holdout days) gives 16.5 ± 3.3c. A game bootstrap of $ a game gives a 5-95% range of $1.58-3.69.

What weakens it:
- Execution at the worst quote in the next minute: 10.3 ± 2.8c and $1.98 a game.
- All games at the worst quote: 7.5 ± 3.0c.
- All games at the worst quote with a 120 s feed lag: only 3.7 ± 3.1c.
- Depth is the main unknown. If fills are capped at what other takers actually printed at our price, from 1 min before to 2 min after the signal, $ a game falls to $1.16 ± 0.42 at the $5 clip. Others printed 10 or more contracts within 2 min only 32% of the time.
- The holdout is effectively February 2026: 394 of 416 trades.
- The top 10% of games carry about half the profit, not all of it; 37 of 141 traded games lose.
- It is still one season of history: Kalshi's first season of women's basketball, untested live, with ESPN's live delay for women's basketball not measured.
verdicts.corrected:

- Base case: 16.5 ± 2.7c a contract (SE clustered by game; 3.3c clustered by day), 416 trades in 141 of 234 games.
- $ a game: $2.57 ± 0.65 at a $5 clip, $1.59 ± 0.40 at a $2 clip.
- Paying the worst price of the next minute: 10.3 ± 2.8c, $1.98 a game.

verdicts.name: Finnish Liiga hockey: goal-triggered pick-off of stale quotes (IOC)
verdicts.reasoning:
The headline number reproduces exactly. The data checks out: 10 re-pulled liiga.fi games are identical and 8 re-pulled Kalshi games match (1,168 trades, 3,036 candles). The calibration is confirmed (lambda 5.346 and OT share 0.675 from 2025-26), and so are the fees.

The 3-hour fix is right in direction and size. Shifting the 2026-27 logTimes by +3 h is the only whole-hour shift that lines goals up with Kalshi price moves (8.7c move; every other shift is about 0). 2025-26 needs no shift. After the fix the market starts moving about 60 s before logTime, so there is no look-ahead. My independent rule on 2026-27 (81 games) gives:
- L=15 s: 16.3 ± 2.1c, 79 trades in 48 games, $0.84 a game at a $5 clip.
- L=60 s: 15.1 ± 2.5c.
- Day-clustered SE: 1.9c over 19 days.

But the claim that the gain is specific to the minutes after a goal does not survive controls on the same month:
(1) A periodic scan at least 5 min after the last goal, buying the leader, earns 13.1 ± 3.4c (n=131). Buying the tied or trailing side loses (-9.1c, -16.4c). The hunters' periodic check pooled all three cases, which hid this.
(2) A rule with no score feed at all, buying the in-game favourite at the ask at fixed times, earns +7.6 ± 3.1c in 2026-27. Favourites won 90% of the time at an average cost of 0.81.
(3) The rule's own trades won 92% against the model's 86%. Realized 16.5c against a model-implied 10.4c, so part of the result is a month in which leaders held on.

The earlier season contradicts it. In 2025-26 (Feb-May 2026) I kept only goals with credible timestamps (465 goals; the market response curve looks like 2026-27's). The rule fires only 0.21 times a game against 0.9, and earns 0.1 ± 8.9c over 25 trades (win rate 76% against 87% predicted). The price-only favourite rule loses 9.5 ± 4.0c that season.

Capacity is small. Others printed 10 or more contracts at our price within 2 min only 18% of the time. Capping fills at what others printed gives $0.59 ± 0.14 a game even in the favourable month. Only 28% of signals were quotes unchanged since before the goal.
